newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Alfa puts catastrophe reinsurance at $8.5 mln.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Alfa puts catastrophe reinsurance at $8.5 mln.

text.p: Alfa Corp said on Tuesday its catastrophe reinsurance expenditures were expected to reach about $8.5 million, or $0.13 a share, in 1996.
The company said in a statement the estimate arose because the boards of directors of the Alfa Insurance Group approved an amendment to the inter-company property-casualty pool.
The amendment calls for allocating catastrophe costs among the members of the pool to reflect the economics of catastrophe finance.
"The change will reduce the catastrophe exposure of Alfa Corp and benefit each member of the group and Alfa's policyholders," the statement said.

"Alfa Corp catastrophe reinsurance expenditures are expected to be about $8.5 million or $0.13 per share in 1996. The company will finalize its reinsurance buying decision for 1997 in the next two months but believes that with this change Alfa Corp can significantly reduce its reinsurance expenses."
